newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to support Hidalgo coffee growers plight.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to support Hidalgo coffee growers plight.

text.p: Mexican coffee farmers in the central state of Hidalgo will receive financial support for losses sustained during a recent frost that affected crops, the Agriculture Ministry said Thursday.
Francisco Velarde Garcia, Hidalgo's Agriculture Ministry delegate, said 2,257 hectares of high-altitude crops had been damaged to varying degrees. He gave no specifics.

Hidalgo has coffee grown on around 43,000 hectares. It is one of Mexico's secondary growing states and in 1994-1995 produced 149,630 60-kg bags out of a total of 4,169,700 bags in the whole country, according to the Mexican Coffee Council.
Velarde said the government would put into action a temporary rural employment program for the growers.
He said cash disbursements will total 1.226 million pesos and that 1.184 million pesos would be spent on the construction of coffee drying patios.
A further 1.34 million pesos will be paid out for work on damaged coffee trees and for plant preparatory work, Velarde said.
He added the aim was to raise coffee yields in the state above the average four to five 100-lb (46/kg) bags per hectare currently achieved.
